sections.h2: How does property tax work for a house in Cabarrus County?
sections.html:
Cabarrus County values every parcel at market value as of January 1, then sends one bill that combines the county rate with any city, town and fire district rates that apply to the address. The county's Revaluation FAQ says each property was valued at fair market value as of January 1, 2024, with no flat percentage change applied to prior assessments.

The tax office lists three building blocks for a parcel's value: the land, the building (type, age and physical characteristics) and extras such as garages, sheds, pools, fences and driveways. Improvements under construction are valued partially, based on percent complete on January 1, and those values feed the bill.

A county adopts its own reappraisal schedule within the limits of G.S. 105-286, which demands a reappraisal at least every eight years. Cabarrus County has chosen a four-year schedule so values track the market more closely.

sections.h2: Who do I contact about assessments and appeals in Cabarrus County?
sections.html:
The Tax Administration department handles assessment and appeals, and the Revaluation office answers value questions at 704-920-2126 or revalinfo@cabarruscounty.us. The office is at 65 Church Street S in Concord, NC 28025, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The Collections side bills and collects for every jurisdiction in the county, which the county's rate page counts as the county itself, seven cities or towns and 16 fire districts. The Equalization and Review Board hears appeals, and its members are appointed by the County Commissioners from residents who know the local real estate market.

  • Real estate values and property cards: the county's online real estate search, by name, address or parcel
  • Comparable sales: a map-based comparable sales tool on the Tax Revaluation page
  • Relief programs: homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker, plus present use value and wildlife conservation programs
  • Payment plans: the Collections office

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Cabarrus County property value?
sections.html:
Start with a written request for an informal review, then move to the Board of Equalization and Review if the answer does not satisfy you. The county says nothing specific is required to start a review, but the more evidence you attach, the stronger the case. The appraiser for your area looks at what you send and responds with an Informal Review notice, which also explains how to go to the formal level.

You get 30 days from that response notice to continue the appeal. A board hearing request goes to Cabarrus County Tax Revaluation, PO Box 707, Concord, NC 28026-0707, or through the county's online system. It must reach the Office of the County Assessor within 30 days of the date on your Notice of Real Estate Assessed Value letter, or any time before the Board adjourns, which the county says usually happens in late April and is advertised in the local newspaper.

After you submit, you and the county appraiser get one more chance to review the case, and you complete an Application for Hearing form. The board hears evidence from both sides and mails a decision letter within 30 days of the hearing. If you still disagree, you may appeal to the NC Property Tax Commission. Under G.S. 105-290, that notice of appeal is filed within 30 days after the board mailed its decision.

One caution from the county itself: the size of the jump between two revaluations is not a valid reason for appeal. Compare your parcel to similar sales instead.

sections.h2: When are Cabarrus County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are due September 1, and they are past due if not paid before the following January 5, according to the Collections page. Real estate, business and individual personal property bills are mailed annually and arrive toward the end of July. The county's FAQ puts the mailing at the end of July or the first part of August.

Cabarrus County tax calendar from county Collections and Revaluation pages
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value date for each parcel; the bill goes to the owner on this date
JanuaryPersonal property listing form is available; real estate changes are listed on it
Late AprilBoard of Equalization and Review usually adjourns
By June 30Tax rates set through the budget process
Late July to early AugustBills mailed
September 1Taxes due
After January 5Bill is delinquent and open to collection or foreclosure

State law sets interest at 2 percent for January 6 to February 1, then three-fourths of one percent a month after that (G.S. 105-360). The county notes that a delinquent bill faces collection actions or tax foreclosure. Collections will work out a payment plan, but the bill must still be paid in full by the delinquent date, and the taxpayer has to ask for the plan, ideally early in the year.

sections.h2: What are the Cabarrus County tax rates?
sections.html:
The county rate for 2026 is $0.576 per $100 of assessed value, and each city or town and fire district adds its own rate. The county's rate page works through an example for a Kannapolis address, adding the Kannapolis rate of $0.5595 to the county rate to reach a combined 2026 rate of $1.1355 per $100.

Rates are set during the budget process, with the Board of Commissioners and each municipality adopting theirs no later than June 30, and the final numbers are usually settled by June. Changes in assessed value may or may not change your bill, because the effect is unknown until the rates are adopted. If you want your own figure, use the county's real estate search for the assessed value and the rate page for each district that covers your parcel, then ask Collections to confirm.

sections.h2: What property tax relief can a Cabarrus County homeowner get?
sections.html:
The county's Tax Revaluation page lists three relief tracks, homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker, all applied for with the county assessor. Under G.S. 105-277.1, the elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or half of the home's appraised value for owners who are 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, with income under the yearly limit. The Department of Revenue's form shows that limit as $38,800 for 2026.

  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit printed on the state form
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4.0% of income at or under the limit and 5.0% above it up to $58,200 for 2026, with a five year ownership and occupancy test and deferred tax
  • Application: Form AV-9 with the assessor, accepted through June 1 before the tax year, and an owner may use only one of the three programs

Farm, forest and wildlife landowners should also ask about the present use value programs, which the county lists separately with applications.

sections.h2: What should a Cabarrus County seller do about property tax at closing?
sections.html:
Pay the current year's tax through the closing, because the lien attaches as of January 1 and follows the parcel under G.S. 105-355. The bill is issued in the owner's name as of January 1, and the county tells sellers who sold during the year to forward the bill to the new owner.

The Cabarrus County market adds context. Census Bureau QuickFacts lists a median owner-occupied home value of $354,800 for 2020-2024, a population estimate of 249,725 for July 2025 and an owner-occupied rate of 71.2 percent. Values in the county's real estate search are set as of January 1, 2024, so compare yours with recent neighborhood sales before you list. Ask the closing attorney for a payoff of all taxes due, including fire district amounts, and ask Collections for the delinquent status of any prior year.

faqs.q: When are Cabarrus County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. The county says a bill is past due if not paid before the following January 5, and state law starts interest on January 6. Bills are mailed toward the end of July.

faqs.q: How often does Cabarrus County revalue real estate?
faqs.a: Every four years by local choice, although state law only requires every eight. The current values are as of January 1, 2024. The Revaluation office at 704-920-2126 can confirm the next cycle.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Cabarrus County property value?
faqs.a: Submit a written request for an informal review, then appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review within 30 days of your value notice or before the board adjourns, usually in late April. The decision letter arrives within 30 days of the hearing.

faqs.q: Can I set up a payment plan for Cabarrus County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The Collections office works with taxpayers on payment plans, but you must request one and the bill still has to be paid in full by the delinquent date. Contacting them early in the year is preferred.

faqs.q: What happens to the tax bill if I sell my Cabarrus County house mid-year?
faqs.a: The bill still goes out in the name of the owner on January 1, so forward it to the buyer if you receive it after closing. Settle the current year's tax through closing so it does not turn into a lien problem for the new owner.
